items.title: Paul Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: He was a master of Bach on a five manual organ... he would give me a real legit 45 minute lesson. He would never play anything for me... I could play it back at him.

ctx.x: Not Paderewski, but — so they thought well maybe he’s got a little talent. And between the two of them I should have. And they gave me lessons starting at eight. I took lessons from the time I was eight until sixteen, and at sixteen I just kind of went on my own from there on. And the teacher I owe most of it to I mean was a guy named Royal Brown who was the city organist at San Diego. And I used to take a lesson after he got through with his afternoon concerts. He used to play “The Well Tempered Clavichord”…
Did he discover this up front, where you demonstrated that ability and he decided that’s not what we need here.
